# Metrics

<!-- GENERATED by `python -m skolyoz_metrics render` from metrics/results.json and metrics/benchmarks/*.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

_Last updated 2026-10-31._ Every number carries a status. 'reported' = taken from the project's own write-ups and not re-run here (it needs private data). 'measured' = produced by a command in this repository. 'not_measured' / 'unvalidated' = known gaps, listed on purpose.

**Read before quoting any number:** the accuracy figures describe offline experiments on web-sourced images. They are not clinical validation and not on-device results. This is a screening aid, not a diagnostic tool.

## 1. Accuracy

### Evaluation protocols

The accuracy tables come from two protocols. They are not interchangeable: read the protocol line under each table.

**`cv5_stage2` — 5-fold cross-validation of Stage 2, out-of-fold** (337 images, 1,582 landmarks; model: 7-landmark Stage 2 (MobileNetV3-small + heatmap + soft-argmax), PyTorch). Images are grouped by similarity (threshold 0.85) so that near-duplicates never straddle folds. Each fold trains on the other four and is measured on images its model never saw; best-epoch selection uses the fold's own validation part, not the measured part. Stage-2 crops are cut around the label with a uniform random offset of up to 35 px in x and y, simulating Stage-1 localisation error. Source: docs/tr/TEKNIK_DOKUMAN.md sections 5.5, 6.1, 6.2; scripts/40_rafinaj7_egit.py (JITTER = 35).

**`holdout50` — Single held-out test split** (50 images; model: Two-stage pipeline, PyTorch (earlier 2-landmark generation; the source does not state the model generation of the decision table separately)). 337 cleaned images split 236 / 51 / 50 (train / val / test) by similarity group. The test split is used once for reporting. Source: docs/tr/MOBIL_YAPILACAKLAR.md section 2 and Phase 1.

### 1.1 Landmark localisation

Protocol `cv5_stage2` (337 images) · Status: `reported` · Source: docs/tr/TEKNIK_DOKUMAN.md section 6.1 · Reproduce: `python scripts/45_rafinaj7_cv.py --kat 5`; `python scripts/46_cv_omurga_analiz.py`. Needs private data.

| Landmark | n | Median (px) | p90 (px) | Label noise floor (px) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Axillary | 674 | 3.045 | 7.518 | 2.45 |
| C7 | 182 | 11.772 | 31.553 | — |
| Sacrum | 180 | 11.345 | 25.354 | — |
| Spine | 546 | 20.489 | 41.958 | 5.58 |

- Errors are in pixels of the 640 x 640 stretched training images.
- The label noise floor for axillary points is the measured disagreement between independent labels of the same photo; for spine points (5.58) it is a leave-one-out upper bound estimated without relabelling.
- Natural spread between folds is 2.1 px: differences smaller than that between two configurations are not statistically meaningful.

### 1.2 Angle measurement

Protocol `cv5_stage2` (337 images) · Status: `reported` · Source: docs/tr/TEKNIK_DOKUMAN.md section 6.2 · Reproduce: `python scripts/45_rafinaj7_cv.py --kat 5`; `python scripts/46_cv_omurga_analiz.py`. Needs private data.

| Measurement | Median (°) | p90 (°) | Signal, median (°) | Error / signal | Single-label floor (°) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Axillary tilt | 0.271 | 1.237 | 2.21 | 0.12 | 0.435 |
| Coronal balance | 1.292 | 3.385 | 1.71 | 0.76 | — |

Averaging independent labels lowers the floor to 0.232 °.

- Signal is the median absolute value of the quantity across the dataset, i.e. the size of what is being measured. Error / signal is derived from the two columns.
- The single-label noise floor is 0.435 degrees; averaging independent labels lowered it to 0.232 (233 of 337 images carry averaged labels).
- These are Stage-2 errors with simulated coarse seeds, NOT an end-to-end measurement with real Stage-1 outputs and NOT an on-device measurement.

### 1.3 Screening decision

Protocol `holdout50` (50 images) · Status: `reported` · Source: docs/tr/MOBIL_YAPILACAKLAR.md section 2 (test, n = 50) · Reproduce: `python scripts/20_tam_degerlendirme.py`; `python scripts/26_tflite_degerlendirme.py`. Needs private data.

| Tilt threshold | Positives | Recall (95 % Wilson CI) | Accuracy (95 % Wilson CI) | Macro-F1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3° | 16 | 15/16 = 0.938 (0.717–0.989) | 44/50 = 0.880 (0.762–0.944) | 0.870 |
| 5° | 6 | 5/6 = 0.833 (0.436–0.970) | 46/50 = 0.920 (0.812–0.968) | 0.834 |
| 7° | 4 | 4/4 = 1.000 (0.510–1.000) | 50/50 = 1.000 (0.929–1.000) | 1.000 |

- Provenance correction: the previous README attributed this table to the 5-fold cross-validation. The same figures appear in MOBIL_YAPILACAKLAR.md under the n = 50 test split, and '15 of 16 positives' cannot come from a 337-image evaluation, so they are filed here as held-out n = 50 results. Re-run scripts/20 to confirm.
- Wilson 95 % intervals are computed from the counts at render time. With 4 to 16 positives they are wide: the 7 degree row (4 of 4) cannot support any claim.
- Thresholds apply to the axillary tilt, which is a surface-asymmetry indicator, not a Cobb angle.

### 1.4 What the second stage buys

Protocol `holdout50` (50 images) · Status: `reported` · Source: docs/tr/MOBIL_YAPILACAKLAR.md section 2 · Reproduce: `python scripts/20_tam_degerlendirme.py`; `python scripts/26_tflite_degerlendirme.py`. Needs private data.

| Metric | Stage 1 only | Stage 1 + 2 | Label floor | Gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Keypoint error, median | 24.35 px | 3.55 px | 2.45 px | 6.9× |
| Keypoint error, mean | 27.37 px | 7.83 px | — | 3.5× |
| Angle error, median | 2.094° | 0.38° | 0.23° | 5.5× |
| Angle error, p90 | 4.742° | 1.706° | — | 2.8× |
| PCK@5px | 5 % | 72 % | — | +67 pp |
| PCK@10px | 18 % | 90 % | — | +72 pp |

- Stage 1 alone gave the same ~24 px error on train, validation and test, i.e. it could not even fit its own training data: the bottleneck is the representation, not the amount of data.
- 10 % of points still deviate by more than 10 px; the tail is mostly bent or atypical poses.

| full_integer_int8 | 3.58 | — | — | — | No detection on 50 of 50 images: one shared output scale (3.59) squeezes confidence (0 to 1) into ~0.3 quantisation steps, so nothing passes the 0.25 threshold. |

### 3.2 Reported from a physical device

Redmi Note 9 Pro, Android 12 (API 31) · Status: `reported` · Source: docs/tr/MOBIL_YAPILACAKLAR.md Phase 2

| Shutter-latency change | Total (ms) |
|---|---|
| baseline (MAXIMIZE_QUALITY, JPEG decoded on the main thread) | 1100 |
| JPEG decode moved to a background thread, decoded with inSampleSize | 950 |
| CAPTURE_MODE_ZERO_SHUTTER_LAG | 588 |

IMU sampling period 19.1 ms; rotation-induced error at 30 °/s fell from 0.3 ° (nearest sample) to < 0.01 ° (interpolation).

- Shutter latency is the time from pressing the shutter to a delivered frame. It is not model inference time.
- The interpolated figure is an upper bound ('< 0.01') measured in a unit test, not on the device.
- Reducing the capture resolution from 12 MP to ~3 MP was expected to shorten JPEG encoding; that was not verified.

### 3.3 Kotlin pre-processing on a desktop JVM

Status: `measured` · Source: ./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest --tests '*PerformansTest*' on 2026-10-31 (desktop JVM, Android Studio JBR 17, 11th Gen Intel Core i7-11800H); PerformansTest.kt

| Step | Mean (ms) |
|---|---|
| Pillow-compatible bilinear downscale, 3000 x 4000 -> 640 x 640 | 104.9 |
| two 128 x 128 crops | 0.6 |
| two input tensors (Stage 1 and Stage 2 normalisation) | 2.8 |
| two soft-argmax readouts | 0.3 |
| total, excluding TFLite | 108.6 |

- Mean of 5 repetitions on a desktop JIT-compiled JVM, including warm-up; not Android runtime (ART) timings.
- The app captures at about 3 MP rather than the 12 MP simulated here, which shrinks the downscale cost; the effect was not measured.
- Compare with the model-only forward time in 3.1: pre-processing is not negligible next to inference.

## 4. Port correctness (Kotlin ↔ Python)

Status: `reported` · Source: docs/tr/MOBIL_YAPILACAKLAR.md Phase 3; android/app/src/test; tests/test_golden_parity.py

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| JVM unit tests | 42 |
| Instrumented (device) tests | 4 |
| Golden rows (olcum / cikarim / kucultme) | 18 / 38 / 6 |
| Acceptance tolerance | 0.05 ° |
| Reported max difference | 0.000 px / 0.0000 ° |

- Expected values in the golden CSVs are generated by running the Python reference (scripts/23_altin_veri.py), not written by hand, so the two implementations cannot share a wrong sign convention unnoticed.
- The 0.000 px / 0.0000 degree figure was obtained on a real phone photograph with an identical 640 x 640 input tensor, i.e. it compares the Kotlin and Python measurement and pre-processing code, not model inference.
- The 4 instrumented tests need a physical device and are not run in CI.
- All 42 JVM tests were run on 2026-10-31 with Gradle 8.10.2 and JDK 17: 42 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. The 42 includes PerformansTest, a timing test with a very loose bound, and a test of the uncalibrated Cobb placeholder (see gaps).

## 5. Robustness

Status: `reported` · Source: docs/tr/MOBIL_YAPILACAKLAR.md Phase 3.5

| Item | Value | Context |
|---|---|---|
| Confidence-gate rejection rate | 5 of 101 measurements (5.0 %) | validation + test images |
| Confidence gate on phone photos | 3 of 3 rejected | three consecutive captures of one scene |
| Phone-photo repeatability (no gate) | 1.25, 3.37, 6.73 degrees | same scene, three consecutive frames |
| Stage 1 stability | 0.4 to 2.5 px | 1/255 input perturbation |
| Stage 2 stability | up to 16.8 px | 1/255 input perturbation |
| Pitch rejection threshold | \|pitch\| > 8 degrees | perspective guard, shutter locked |

- The gate does not improve the model; it turns silently wrong answers into visible rejections. The root cause is the domain gap between web-sourced training images and phone photographs.
- The gate has not yet been exercised on a real capture campaign.

## 7. Negative results

Status: `reported` · Source: docs/tr/TEKNIK_DOKUMAN.md sections 6.3 and 6.4

| Approach | Result | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Spine trace by image processing (shadow valley) | Residual RMS 9.20 % of torso height; 2 of 110 images gave a usable trace. | The lowest-intensity point is usually a scapula edge or side shadow, not the spinal groove. |
| Polynomial fit to average out landmark noise | Apex-deviation error / signal = 1.01 (degree 3). | Landmark errors are correlated, so the curve moves with the error. |
| Reduce to 3 landmarks (C7, mid-spine, sacrum) | Convexity-direction accuracy fell from 0.639 to 0.550 (chance baseline 0.494). | — |
| Hand-made orientation heuristics | Silhouette-width profile agreed with the colour cue 50 % of the time (chance). | Skin-tone centroid gives no signal on greyscale images. |
| Spine curvature profile (goal H5) | Lateral error 5.88 px vs label floor 5.58 px vs signal 6.50 px; convexity accuracy 63.9 % vs 52.8 % for always guessing the majority class. | The limit is label quality, not the model. |
| Single-stage direct coordinate regression | About 24 px error on train, validation and test alike. | Representation, not data volume. |

## 8. Known gaps

Things this project has **not** measured or validated. They are listed on purpose; a metrics page without them would overstate what is known.

| Id | Status | What | Why it is open | Next step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `on_device_inference_latency` | not_measured | Latency of Stage 1 + 7 x Stage 2 on a phone, and RAM, energy and thermal behaviour. | Only shutter latency was ever measured on the device. scripts/31 prints a ~100-200 ms target but that was written when the pipeline refined 2 points, not 7. | Run the benchmark protocol in docs/BENCHMARKING.md on at least one low-end and one mid-range phone. |
| `end_to_end_accuracy` | not_measured | Accuracy of the full chain with real Stage-1 outputs for all 7 landmarks. | The cross-validation seeds Stage 2 with simulated (+-35 px) offsets instead of real Stage-1 predictions. | Out-of-fold Stage 1 as well, then evaluate the chain on the out-of-fold images. |
| `tflite_accuracy_7_landmarks` | not_measured | Quantisation cost of the 7-landmark TFLite models. | Measured only for the 2-landmark models (about +0.04 degrees). | Extend scripts/26 to the 7-landmark pipeline. |
| `phone_photo_accuracy` | not_measured | Accuracy on photographs captured with a phone under the intended protocol. | Training and evaluation images are web-sourced; the phone data amounts to a handful of informal captures. | Collect 200-300 protocol-conformant phone photos with a second independent labelling round. |
| `cobb_estimate` | unvalidated | The Cobb-angle estimate and risk category shown on the Android overlay (Kalibrasyon.cobbTahmini, scripts/48_cobb_kalibrasyon.py). | Its coefficients (1.25 / 1.10 / 2.40) and the '+-3.5 degree' error margin are not fitted to any radiograph-matched data - none exists in this project - and contradict the project's own rule that the interface must not state a Cobb angle. Treat it as a placeholder, not a measurement. | Remove it from the UI, or gate it behind a debug flag, until it is calibrated on radiograph-paired data. |
